jobs.summary: Delete the empty `note-images` storage bucket from the Supabase dashboard
jobs.why: It was created for a synced-notes design that was reversed the same hour: study notes are on-device only. Its four RLS policies are already dropped and it holds zero objects, so nothing can reach it and nothing is at risk — but an empty private bucket is a thing every future reader has to reason about before concluding it is dead. Briefly declined on 2026-09-01 and then asked for again once the owner knew what it was; that is the whole reason a decision belongs in this file rather than in a chat message. SQL cannot remove it: storage.protect_delete() raises 42501 on any direct delete from the storage tables, and that guard should be respected rather than disabled. supabase-tasks.yml now has a step that does it through the Storage API, which refuses a non-empty bucket of its own accord.
jobs.verify: select count(*) from storage.buckets where id='note-images' returns 0.

jobs.summary: Deploy generate-handwritten-notes so every Physiology note is guaranteed a flowchart (live is v52)
jobs.why: Physiology is examined on mechanism — reflex arcs, feedback loops, conduction pathways — so the flowchart is the section a student writes down. The system prompt only ASKS for one conditionally, and 3 of the 11 Physiology notes in the cache came back without it. The payload adds a subject-scoped prompt rule plus ensurePhysiologyFlowchart(), which runs at every point that writes to handwritten_notes (single-note upsert, saveContent, persisted AI edit) and makes one targeted call for the missing section. It is allowed to refuse: a question with no sequence in it gets no flowchart, because an invented one is a wrong answer the student copies onto paper. Deploy BOTH files in pending-deploy/ as generate-handwritten-notes/index.ts and generate-handwritten-notes/textbook.ts — a deploy replaces every file, and textbook.ts is byte-identical to v52. Then DELETE pending-deploy/, which is a payload and not a checkout.
jobs.verify: get_edge_function generate-handwritten-notes → version > 52 and the source contains `ensurePhysiologyFlowchart`. Triple-tap a Physiology question with no cached note and confirm the flowchart is on the page. Then `cd mobile && npm run notes:physio-flowchart` for the plan (3 notes, 3 calls) and `-- --run` to backfill the cached ones.
jobs.outcome: Deployed. Live is v56, not the v53 this job was written against, because deploying it exposed two further bugs the queued payload alone would not have fixed. (1) buildFlowchartSection built its section by hand and assumed one exact reply shape, so a model answering in any other shape scored zero steps; it now coerces the shapes a model actually returns (bare strings, {step,description}, steps hoisted, section hoisted) and logs what it received when it still cannot use one. It never invents a step and the >=3 bar holds. (2) The real cause, found only because of that new logging: callModel sent SYSTEM_PROMPT on every call, so the repair asked for ONE flowchart section while the system instruction demanded a whole note — the model obeyed the system prompt and returned a complete note every time. callModel/callGeminiDirect now take an optional system instruction, the repair sends its own, and flowchartSectionFrom reads a whole-note reply's sections as a fallback. Backfill done: the 3 cached Physiology notes that lacked a flowchart now have one (ECG -> Electrical Conduction and ECG Correlation; hypothalamus -> Hypothalamic Regulation of Food Intake; General Physiology -> Na+-K+ Pump). 14 of 14 Physiology notes now carry one, including 3 written by real readers after the deploy, which is the guarantee working unattended. Rows backed up in handwritten_notes_pre_flowchart_backup. Route note: a sandbox CAN reach an edge function with no direct egress — the `http` extension runs the request from Postgres. See .agents/state/blocked.json, blocker `supabase-route`.

jobs.summary: Deploy generate-flashcards so decks stop dying on decorated JSON (live is v15)
jobs.why: Decks are not being built OR cached. `flashcards` has 4 rows, none newer than 27 August, while the function logs show readers generating decks all day. Every run ends `SyntaxError: Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position 6975` in parseJson, which throws long before the upsert at the bottom of the file — so readers pay the full Gemini cost on every open and get an error for it. The `[flashcards] subject=...` log that looks like a success is printed at line 749 and callGemini is at 836; it is a pre-flight log, not a result. Cause: parseJson stripped one leading and one trailing fence then JSON.parse'd the whole remainder, so anything after the array closes killed it. Fixed with extractJson(), which takes the outermost bracket pair the way parseMcqs has in the client since day one. Checked against eight shapes: the new one passes all eight, the shipped one fails six including both real production shapes.
jobs.how: TWO ROUTES, either is fine. (1) Merge this branch to main, then dispatch `.github/workflows/supabase-deploy-functions.yml` with functions=generate-flashcards — it deploys from the repo, byte-identical, and prints every file's size and sha before pushing. GitHub only registers workflow_dispatch from the DEFAULT branch, which is the only reason this was not dispatched already. (2) Or `supabase functions deploy generate-flashcards --project-ref pmtgeydtqypwrypshhsx` from a checkout. Deploying through the MCP connector also works but takes each file's full text as a parameter, and index.ts is 43 KB — an agent retyping that has one silent typo between it and breaking the flagship feature for everyone.
jobs.verify: get_edge_function generate-flashcards -> version > 15 and the source contains `extractJson`. Then generate a deck for a chapter that has none and confirm a NEW row appears: `select deck_key, card_count, created_at from flashcards order by created_at desc limit 3;` should show today. A sandbox can invoke the function without direct egress via the `http` extension from Postgres — see blocker `supabase-route`.
jobs.appliedNote: Deployed by the Deploy Supabase edge functions workflow, run 1 on main at 892207a3 (2026-09-10T18:50Z), which finished green. That workflow could not be dispatched at all until the file reached the default branch — GitHub only registers workflow_dispatch from there — which is why this sat queued.

jobs.summary: Insert the app_releases row for versionCode 22
jobs.why: Older builds read app_releases to offer the update, and the new build reads its own row to say what it fixed. With no row, the in-app update prompt never fires for 22 and the What's New card is empty — which looks exactly like the update feature being broken. Queued rather than applied because this sandbox has no route to Supabase: direct egress is blocked (HTTP 403 at the gateway) and the MCP connector's token expired mid-session. live_on_play stays false until the listing actually serves 22.
